Public domain: every person whose words are in this text died in 1925 or earlier, so the term has ended under the law of every country, whichever one first published it.

People: George Crabbe (author, Wikidata Q903516), died 1834; Adolphus William Ward (editor, Wikidata Q647094), died 1924. They are every person Project Gutenberg's catalog lists for the book ("Crabbe, George, 1754-1832; Ward, Adolphus William, Sir, 1837-1924 [Editor]") and every person the printed edition's opening pages credit; each death year is Wikidata's (Wikidata gives some of them several death years, every one 1925 or earlier: George Crabbe [1832, 1834]).

Printed edition: The poetical works of George Crabbe, London, Oxford university press, H. Frowde, 1908, the Internet Archive scan https://archive.org/details/cu31924013467489. Three passages of the Gutenberg text have 73%, 75%, 92% of their four-word runs in the scan's text. The scan does not show the credit of Adolphus William Ward, whom the catalog lists; the passages show the scan holds this text.
